title: German Confederation
capsule: The German Confederation (Deutscher Bund) was a loose association of 39 sovereign German-speaking states established by the Congress of Vienna in 1815 to replace the dissolved Holy Roman Empire, with its sole institution being the Federal Assembly (Bundesversammlung) at Frankfurt, permanently chaired by Austria. Perpetual rivalry between Austria and Prussia paralyzed the Confederation's executive capacity; the Carlsbad Decrees of 1819 suppressed liberal and nationalist movements across member states, while the Zollverein customs union of 1834, led by Prussia, deepened economic integration outside Austrian influence. The revolutions of 1848–49 briefly dissolved the Assembly before it was reconstituted in 1850 under Austrian pressure. Prussia's victory over Austria in the Seven Weeks' War ended the Confederation at the Peace of Prague in August 1866, after which Prussia organized the North German Confederation.
